messages:
maria: Quick update — ran a small grid (linear / NTK / YARN) across Mistral, Llama, Mixtral for long-context stability. Wanted to dump results and get quick eyes.
jonathan: awesome, did you use the new kernel picker heuristics or forced kernel?
maria: kernel picker. Default picks FFT path for Mixtral beyond 32k in our infra. We also tried forcing GEMM for comparison.
priya: did you keep the batching heuristic the same? e.g., max_batch_tokens=4096 + dynamic windowing?
maria: yes same batching profile. Only varied RoPE variant + kernel.
kevin: TL;DR? any perf cliff or perplexity regression?
maria: mixed. Llama stable across variants up to 64k. Mistral shows mild perplexity drift with YARN after ~48k but no huge spikes. Mixtral w/ NTK + FFT shows a sharp perplexity jump (~2.3 ppl) at 65k->70k.
jonathan: yikes. spike reproducible? seeds? prompt mix?
maria: reproducible on deterministic eval prompts (long wikipedia passages). Re-ran w/ 5 seeds, CI < 0.1 for the jump.
perf-bot: Profiling link: https://perf.redwood/internal/ops/2418007777 (contains timeline, kernel breakdown, memcopy heatmap) :chart_with_upwards_trend:
priya: looking at the profile: headKV memcpy + kernel switch overhead lines up with the spike window. We're thrashing KV eviction when FFT path tries to allocate temp buffers.
kevin: does forcing GEMM avoid the spike for Mixtral?
maria: yes — forcing GEMM keeps perplexity smooth but latency increases ~12% and tail P95 goes up. So it's a quality vs latency trade.
jonathan: could be numerical with NTK scaling + FFT path post-scaling rounding? Maybe accumulation order changes. Any difference if we run 32-bit vs 16-bit?
maria: tried fp16 vs bf16: bf16 slightly better but spike persists. fp32 removes it (but expensive).
priya: code snippet of the command used:
```
./perf-runner --model mixtral-v1 --rope ntk --kernel auto --ctx 70000 --batch 8 --dtype bf16 --evalset long_wiki
```
kevin: interesting. If fp32 removes spike, sounds like a cancellation/precision issue introduced by new kernel math. Could we add a numerically stable fallback only for contexts > 64k?
jonathan: feasible: add cheap sanity check on a small prompt window (prefix) to compare logits between primary kernel and a reference kernel for drift. If drift > threshold, switch to GEMM for rest of request.
priya: That matches our fallback policy idea. But need to be careful with overhead — running reference could double some work. Maybe compare on first 512 tokens only.
maria: also saw throughput regression in throughput logs when kernel switches mid-request — batching scheduler treats switch as incompatible and breaks continuous batching, causing latency spike.
kevin: scheduler should allow kernel-agnostic batching where possible. But if kernel requires different workspace layout, we might have to flush. Can we pre-declare kernel per model+ctx to avoid mid-request changes?
jonathan: yes, add kernel binding based on per-model safe range table. We can compute safe ranges offline via grid (what you just ran) and store in model profiles.
priya: I exported a quick safe-range draft: Llama: up to 96k for linear/NTK; Mistral: linear up to 64k, YARN safe up to 48k; Mixtral: GEMM preferred above 60k, NTK unstable 65k+. (attached CSV to perf link)
maria: exact numbers in the perf link -> the CSV has per-variant perplexities and latencies.
kevin: next steps? ops + infra?
maria: propose: 1) add per-model safe-range metadata to model catalog (make kernel_picker consult it) 2) implement light sanity check on first 512 tokens if kernel != catalog default 3) update scheduler to avoid mid-request kernel churn where possible 4) rerun grid with quantized kernels to see interactions.
jonathan: + add a test in eval-harness to catch >0.5 ppl drift on longctx across kernels.
priya: also check KV cache eviction thresholds — I suspect our eviction policy reduces slot reuse when FFT workspace hits high-water mark. Maybe we should prefer prefix-KV pinning when ctx > threshold.
kevin: agree. For immediate mitigation, set Mixtral NTK off for >60k in hosted defaults and add note to release.
maria: I'll open a PR for model profile changes and a ticket for scheduler changes. Assigning: @jonathan scheduler, @priya KV heuristics, @kevin release note + hosted defaults.
jonathan: grabbing scheduler ticket.
priya: starting KV heuristics triage now.
kevin: will draft release note and update hosted config.
maria: thanks all. Will paste the grid CSV and a minimal reproducer in the ticket. Quick aside: anyone seen similar NTK instabilities on Mixtral with long repetitive numeric sequences?
jonathan: we saw something similar in 202 where periodic patterns caused resonance in attention. Might be related.
priya: good call — I'll add pattern-based prompt tests to the eval harness.
kevin: :thumbsup: any objections to immediate Mixtral NTK soft-disable above 60k?
jonathan: +1
priya: +1
perf-bot: Automated ticket created: PERF-9843 (maria) — rope-grid sanity check + scheduler fallback
maria: ok wrapping. I'll drop follow-ups in the ticket. Thanks!
